exact_statement: For every integer n>=3, let F(x,a,b,z)=(-1)^a on x=0 and 1-2*1[b=1,z=0] on x=1, with independent fair physical bits. Starting with the FULL product of root Fourier marginals, query a and actually reset both Bayes references to their actual products. With m=n+2,d=2^(1-m), the uncovered first-conversion excess is D_m=h2(d)+H(point_(m-1))/2-H(point_m), and 0<D_m<h2(d)<3/5 bits. After any adaptive sequence and stopping rule querying only distinct private z bits and actually resetting to actual products at every queried node, all subsequent signed product resets are nonpositive (at active dimension l>=6, sigma_l<=-2*2^(1-l)). A single original global allocation of one bit from the a=1 child S4=4I-H pays an explicitly booked prior global debit 1/4 and the first actual excess, carrying conditional debit 1/2+2D_m unchanged into every descendant; every stopping frontier retains at least 3/20 global bit of this allocation. Both branches retain full terminal H, influence and current reference KL. The n=2 boundary has negative D_4 and is covered using [D_4]_+=0. This is a source-specific exercised-reset ledger, not a universal FEI or occupancy-reference theorem.
